title: SC08 candidate-quarantine.schema.json -- Stage 2 inert candidate area (06-PROMOTION-POLICY.md §4 five implementation requirements + CM-32)
description: The document S11 kd_quarantine emits for one inert candidate area, and the record shape of each quarantined candidate inside it. Writer: S11 (12-SKILL-DESIGN-BRIEF.md:184). Validators: S09 kd_validate (the sole witness, 12:171) and S10 kd_gate in Wave 3. The five requirements of 06:177 each own at least one field here, so a schema that passed without them could not describe a real Stage 2 quarantine: (1) pending storage -> candidates[].pending_file; (2) artifact hash -> candidates[].sha256 + candidates[].artifact_hash; (3) conflict refusal -> conflicts[] rows whose action is const suppressed_by_pending (06:189); (4) approve/apply in one transaction -> there is deliberately NO approval state in a candidate record, because the only carrier is the emitted one-transaction bundle ($defs.apply_bundle, 06:247); (5) Rejected and Failed kept apart -> rejected and failed are two blocks over two different ledger files (06:195).

schema_version.description: SC08's own version. Bumped only when the field set changes, so a consumer can tell a stale reader from a new writer.

at.description: The instant captured ONCE for this call and reused for every row this document renders (05-DATA-MODEL.md §2: 时间戳取一次). A per-field clock would make the report's own rows disagree.

root.description: Absolute, symlink-resolved quarantine root. Resolved rather than as-given because 06's placement demand is about where the bytes really are, not about how the caller spelled them: `../` and a symlink must not be able to move a candidate into a skills root.

inertness.description: The placement verdict for this root. It is part of the document, not a side log, so a report cannot be forwarded without the evidence that the area is unloadable.

pending_count.description: How many candidates are live right now: state pending AND bytes present AND not expired. Derived from disk on every call and never stored, which is what keeps quarantine from becoming a second authority (05 §1 红线 1/2, CM-11/CM-13). Rejected and failed candidates are excluded by definition -- that exclusion is the observable form of 06:195's separation.

hint.description: The operator-facing notice that goes with the count. Contract S11 pins only the coupling, and the allOf below states it mechanically: an empty queue renders an empty string, a non-empty queue renders a non-empty string. Round 2 nowhere adjudicates the wording, so the emitted string is the plainest possible one and carries no emoji, no severity and no count -- see the IMPLEMENTATION_GAP in the writer's docstring and in W2-C-REPORT.md. A consumer that rendered a default hint over an empty queue would be reproducing the 无写入者字段 rendered as real data defect of 05-DATA-MODEL.md §5.4 (3).

candidates.description: Every candidate record in the area, sorted by candidate_id. Includes the non-live ones (rejected, failed, expired, consumed): hiding them would be the 沉默消失 06:197 forbids.

conflicts.description: Requirement 3 of 06:177, made visible: every staged candidate that was refused because its target already had something pending. 06:189's instruction is to record the suppression rather than relax the rule, and 06:197 (run-account-anti-silence) is why the refusal reaches the document instead of only the exit code.

rejected.description: Requirement 5, half one: the human decisions. Its own file, its own row shape.

failed.description: Requirement 5, half two: the attempts that errored. A different carrier from `rejected` on purpose -- 06:200 says the difference is decisional, so one file for both would erase it.

integrity.description: The two ways the area can be half-written. Reported, never repaired: a candidate whose draft bytes vanished is not counted as pending and is not silently dropped, and a draft with no record is an orphan the operator can see (the crash window between writing the draft and writing the record is intentional -- a record without verifiable bytes must never exist).

live_pending.description: The candidate ids behind pending_count, in the same order the count was computed. Without it the number would be an assertion; with it a reader can recompute it from `candidates` and `integrity`.

allOf.$comment: Contract S11, verbatim: `pending_count<=0` 时 hint 必须为空串. Stated in the schema as well as in the writer so that S09 refuses a report that breaks it, and so a future writer cannot loosen the rule by only editing Python. The reverse arm is the second half of the same clause: pending_count>0 with an empty hint is a silent queue. History of the branch key: it was written as `enum: [0]` when kd_validate._walk compared `maximum` with >=, which made an upper bound accept everything above it (W2-C found this while landing SC08). That comparison is fixed and locked by test_bound_keywords_compare_in_the_right_direction, so the clause is now expressed as the adjudicated `maximum: 0`.

inertness.description: CM-32's inertness, as data. `placement_check_ran` is const true because this block only exists when the check ran: a quarantine area is never reachable without a verdict, so a report that skipped the check cannot be rendered at all.

requested_root.description: What the caller asked for, before resolution, so a refusal names the path as given.

host_skills_root.description: True when a path segment is a host-loaded skills/rules surface. The contract forbids the area being there ('惰性候选区读写（**不在宿主 skills 根**）'), because a quarantined file a host reads is an active instruction with a new name.

inside_store_root.description: True when the root sits under a store that S08 declared (an ancestor holding store-layout.json, or an explicit --store-root). Quarantine bytes inside the store would show up as S08's NON_OWNER_WRITE, which is the right outcome -- and the reason S11 refuses it earlier.

corpus_root.description: True when the path runs through the read-only evidence corpus (repos/).

frozen_round.description: True when the path is inside .distill/round-1 or .distill/round-2, which are tagged immutable.

reason_codes.description: NAMED refusals, closed set. A refusal without a name is the 假门 shape again: the operator cannot tell a policy decision from a crash.

ok.description: false only when reason_codes is non-empty; the writer raises instead of producing a report, so an emitted report always has ok true. `not` keeps that link assertible rather than prose.

pending_candidate.description: One quarantined candidate: 06:180's `_pending/<id>.md + sha256 + artifact hash` (requirements 1 and 2) plus the target that requirement 3 keys on. No approval, verdict or evidence field is required here -- approval arrives with the apply call in the same transaction (see $defs.apply_bundle) and a verdict is S10's to write.

candidate_id.description: Doubles as the draft file's name, so the pattern is a path-safety constraint first and an identifier second: no separator, no leading dot, bounded length.

target.description: What the candidate would become. Requirement 3 is per-target (同 target 已有 pending → 拒绝新建), so a candidate without a target cannot be conflict-checked and is refused at the door.

state.description: pending is the only state that counts toward pending_count. rejected/failed are the two accounts of requirement 5 and stay distinct here as well as on disk; consumed means a durable commit was reported for it; expired is 06:190's 过期通道 and only fires when the candidate carries its own expires_at.

pending_file.description: Requirement 1, with 06:180's literal directory name. Relative to the quarantine root, so a record cannot point at a file outside the inert area.

sha256.description: Requirement 2a: the digest of the draft bytes. This is what makes 06:185-186 checkable -- a hand edit to a _pending file is a mismatch, and the tree's requirement on a mismatch is fail-closed refusal plus a failed row.

artifact_hash.description: Requirement 2b: a digest over the canonical artifact triple {target, landing, size_bytes, pending_sha256} via kd_provenance.content_hash. Two digests, not one, because 06:180 names both and they answer different questions: these bytes, versus this proposal. It is also the key of 06:200's re-submission rule.

size_bytes.description: N22b (06:202) requires the model to report the size of what it drafted, and 06:240-242 makes size a budget input that must not be re-guessed later. minimum 1 because an empty draft is refused rather than stored as a placeholder.

staged_at.description: Captured once per call and reused; the same value appears in the rows that call writes.

updated_at.description: Present only when the record left its staged state, so the original staging instant is never overwritten.

expires_at.description: The candidate's own expiry instant (06:190's 过期通道). Absent means it never expires on its own: no default TTL is applied anywhere, because no such value was adjudicated.

landing.description: N22b's SUGGESTED tier/landing point for a draft. Advisory and hashed, never decided on: the authority for the value set is 06 §5.1's terminal states as emitted by S10 in SC12, and duplicating that enum here would make SC08 a second owner of it. The pattern is structural only.

decision_digest.description: PENDING_CONSUMER: S10 kd_gate's verdict digest over this candidate (SC12 `verdict.schema.json`, 12:188; the same name S12 already binds into a store record at commit time). Written by nobody in Wave 2 and read by nobody in Wave 2: S11 does not invent a reader to make it look consumed. Declared here because SC08 is the carrier that outlives the gate.

prior_states.description: N21's per-item watermark in its visible form: a re-submission records what the item was before, so an attempt cannot reset its own history by re-staging under the same id.

suppression_row.description: 06:189: 同 target 已有 pending 即拒会挡掉合法连续修正 -- the disposition is to record it, not to widen the rule. `action` is const so this file cannot quietly collect other event kinds.

seq.description: Position in the append-only file: what makes 'nothing overwrote anything' checkable (06:193 forbids a later failure overwriting the most informative earlier sample).

rejected_row.description: A human decision (06:200: rejected = 人的决定, and 无新证据不得再提). `by` is closed to the human members of SC07's attribution enum, so a model cannot fill the queue with refusals attributed to nobody.

failed_row.description: An attempt that errored, which 06:200 makes retryable -- the opposite of a rejection. `kind` is closed so the reason a candidate left the queue is always one of the named fail-closed cases. `target` and `artifact_hash` are plain strings here rather than 64-hex because a failure can be recorded about a candidate whose record is itself unreadable, and forcing the digest would delete the only evidence that something went wrong.

rowDigest.description: Written by the Wave-0 kernel's append_ledger (kd_provenance.append_ledger prepends a digest over the canonical row), which is the only hook an append-only file offers: it makes an in-place edit of a quarantine account detectable, the same reason SC07 carries it. Declared because SC08's rows ARE the rows that channel writes -- omitting it made this schema refuse the real rows while landing the file, which is the witness doing its job.

apply_bundle.$comment: Requirement 4 of 06:177 (`06:247` N27: approve 与 apply 同事务, 任一步失败则整批不落). Deliberately NOT an instance shape of this document: kd_quarantine.apply_bundle returns this bundle and writes nothing, and the durable half is S12's commit_batch. That is what keeps approve state out of the inert area -- if quarantine stored an approval, an approved-but-never-applied record would be a second, desynchronisable authority over what was consented to.

shape.single_transaction: true, always: one txn_id covers both steps
shape.txn_id: shared by approve_row and apply_intent; a mismatch is refused APPROVE_APPLY_SPLIT
shape.apply_intent: handed to S12 kd_write_txn.commit_batch; S11 has no write rights into the store
shape.pending_release: {candidate_id, txn_id}: the queue drains only for the transaction that was approved

counter_admission.$comment: 05-DATA-MODEL.md §5.4's five conditions, applied to the one counter this schema owns (pending_count): (1) writer = stage_candidate / reject / fail / consume / sweep, each a named call site in kd_quarantine.py; (2) tests = test_w2c_quarantine.py covers 'event happened -> count changed' AND 'count changed -> hint changed' AND 'count changed -> apply refused'; (3) consumer closure = pending_count is rendered into a hint only by hint_for, whose empty branch is the empty string, so a default cannot masquerade as data; (4) lifecycle = 06:190's expiry channel exists per candidate and rejected/failed/consumed leave the count; (5) storage boundary = the count lives in a rendering that is recomputed and deletable, never beside rebuildable index bytes. The count of `rejected`/`failed` rows is not a counter at all: the rows are the account and a consumer counts them if it needs a number.
